name: Sorbitol
aliases: E420, E420(i), E420(ii), E420i, E420ii, INS 420(i), INS 420(ii), sorbitol, sorbitol syrup, D-glucitol, D-glucitol syrup, jarabe de sorbitol
what_is: Sorbitol (INS 420(i)) and sorbitol syrup (INS 420(ii)) are polyols used as bulk sweeteners, humectants and texturising ingredients. Sorbitol also occurs naturally in many fruits, including prunes, pears, apples and peaches.
why_botia: Sorbitol replaces both the sweetness and the bulk of sugar. It also occurs naturally in fruits like prunes, pears, apples and peaches — and its high concentration in prunes is one reason they can have a laxative effect. Little of it is absorbed: the rest draws water into the gut and is fermented, so larger amounts loosen stools. JECFA assigned an ADI “not specified”.
